subject: Chemistry
title: Dalton's Atomic Theory
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Dalton's Atomic Theory.

hook.text: In 1803, John Dalton proposed that each element is made of unique atoms with a specific weight. Modern chemistry began.

buildup.text: Dalton noticed that elements combine in fixed ratios by weight—hydrogen and oxygen always combine as 1:8.

discovery.text: He concluded: atoms of each element are identical, atoms of different elements differ in weight and properties.

twist.text: Dalton was colorblind—literally. He studied his own condition and 'daltonism' became a word for colorblindness.

climax.text: His atomic weights were often wrong, but the concept was revolutionary. Chemistry became quantitative, not qualitative.

punchline.text: Fixed ratios mean fixed atoms. Dalton turned chemistry into a counting science.

quiz.question: What key observation led Dalton to propose atomic theory?
options: Elements combine in fixed ratios by weight
All gases expand at the same rate when heated
Elements have unique colors when burned

details.summary: In 1803 John Dalton proposed that each chemical element consists of identical atoms with a unique weight, and that atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios to form compounds. His theory transformed chemistry from qualitative art into quantitative science.
details.whyItMatters: Dalton's atomic theory gave chemistry its first predictive mathematical framework. It enabled stoichiometry, explained the law of definite proportions, and launched modern quantitative chemistry.
takeaways: Dalton proposed atoms of each element have a characteristic weight
Atoms combine in fixed whole-number ratios in compounds
His theory explained the law of multiple proportions experimentally

faq.question: What was wrong with Dalton's original atomic theory?
faq.answer: Dalton assumed atoms were solid indivisible spheres and that the simplest compound of two elements had a one-to-one ratio. He got water's formula wrong as HO instead of H2O. He also had no concept of subatomic particles or isotopes, which were discovered much later.

faq.question: How did Dalton determine the relative weights of atoms?
faq.answer: He measured the mass ratios of elements in compounds through careful experiments. By assuming the simplest possible formulas, he calculated relative atomic weights. Though his assumptions introduced errors, his approach established the principle that atomic weights are measurable.
